description: issue #954: the handler-firing `instruction` event carries a `handler` discriminator, so registration and firing are told apart by a FIELD rather than by span arithmetic. `spec/interaction-events.md`'s "Trace stream integration" requires both: executing `on_key "space" [ … ]` emits an ordinary statement `instruction` (seq 0) plus the registration `primitive` (seq 1, `:166-168` -- "Event registration forms emit `primitive` events after the handler is registered"), and the delivered press then emits the block-head `instruction` (seq 3, `:148-149` -- "The start of a handler block emits an `instruction` event for the block-head that caused the handler to run"). This fixture is the whole point of #954 in one file: **seq 0 and seq 3 start at the SAME position, line 1 column 1**, carry the same `kind` (`instruction`) and the same `statement_kind` (`ProfileStatement`), and before #954 differed ONLY in their `end` column -- 27 for the whole statement versus 7 for the bare `on_key` keyword. A consumer therefore had to re-derive "is this a registration or a firing?" by comparing span WIDTH, an invariant the spec never states and no fixture asserted; a non-visual surface reading it could announce only `on_key`, indistinguishable from re-running the registration line. Now the answer is the presence of `handler`: **seq 0 has no `handler` key at all** (a registration is an ordinary statement) while **seq 3 carries `{kind: "on_key", key: "space"}`**. That the field also names the KEY is what lets an accessibility surface say "your space-key handler fired" rather than just "a handler fired". The payload carries the handler's **registration-time signature** -- the block-head kind plus the argument it was registered with, evaluated -- and excludes occurrence/dispatch metadata, anything describing WHEN or HOW one firing was delivered; that is the rule recorded on `HandlerFiring` in `@openlogo/core`, and the reason a TICK is deliberately NOT carried here (a tick describes when a firing happened rather than what the handler is, and `spec/interaction-events.md:69-73` makes it "an implementation-defined logical frame" besides). It is a signature and NOT an identifier: duplicate registrations emit an identical payload AND an identical span, so a consumer needing per-registration identity uses `ExecuteOptions.handlerRegistrations` instead. The sibling `on_key/on-key-registered-not-delivered` is the negative control: a registration that never fires produces no `handler` key anywhere in its stream.
